variants.headline: Shipbuilding for the colony route
variants.sub: Shipbuilding by the home world has provided a larger vessel or another vessel for the colony route.
variants.body:
The home world has built a larger ship or an additional ship for the colony route. The construction is a transport development, not an announcement of arrival. In assessing {target}, readers should distinguish provision of a vessel from an unreported schedule, cargo or immediate change in supplies.

The gazette records the construction for the colonial route without describing the vessel as having reached the colony. Completion of a ship and completion of a voyage are distinct administrative facts. A useful notice should also avoid assigning an unreported cargo capacity or timetable to the development.

We remain critical of {target}. A shipbuilding development should not place transport stewardship beyond scrutiny; the colony deserves a demanding standard rather than automatic admiration for the announcement of a vessel. Care in the public record is part of responsible administration.
